ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is the physical connection diagram of student Xiaowen studying the characteristics of current and voltage in a series circuit. When the switch is closed, lamp $L_{1}$ is on, lamp $L_{2}$ is not on, and both the ammeter and the voltmeter have readings. What is the possible cause of this fault?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the upper left of the figure there is a switch, in the middle above is bulb L1, in the upper right an ammeter A is connected in series, and on the right side is the power supply; in the middle below is bulb L2, and in the lower left a voltmeter V is connected. From the connection relationship of the wires it can be seen that L1 and L2 are in the same series circuit, the ammeter is connected in the main circuit, and the voltmeter is also connected into the circuit to carry out voltage measurement. Then reason: after the switch is closed, L1 is on and the ammeter has a reading, indicating that there is current passing through the main circuit, the whole series loop is not an open circuit, and the path where the power supply, switch, ammeter, and L1 are located is basically normal. If L2 is open-circuited, then the series circuit as a whole will have no current, L1 also will not be on, and the ammeter also will not have a reading, so it does not conform to the phenomenon. Now only L2 is not on, while the series path still has current, indicating that the current does not normally pass through L2's filament to emit light; it may be that L2 is shorted by a wire, and the current bypasses L2 and flows through, so L2 is not on while L1 can still emit light.
